answer: The printer's type case holds one font, and the press log records the number of sheets and the date of every run. A basalt page printed elsewhere fails the log. At the jetty of the type the letters must match the case's own wear, and a strange press leaves different marks. Forging a run means buying a press, setting type for a month and paying 17,400. The gale entry in the printer's book is kept for the guild, so a page whose run was never logged is burned.
